words.desc: A large reptile with a broad rounded snout that lives in swamps of the southern United States.
A tiny insect that lives in large organised colonies and can carry heavy loads.
A toothless mammal with a curved muzzle and a sticky tongue used to lap up small colonial insects.
A graceful swift-running African and Asian grazing mammal carrying permanent unbranched horns.
A nocturnal burrowing mammal encased in protective leathery armor plates of overlapping bone.
A stout burrowing carnivore recognized by its striped black and white face and fierce defensive tenacity.
A small winged mammal that hunts at night by listening for echoes to find prey.
A large heavy mammal with thick fur and strong claws that may sleep through winter.
A large rodent with big front teeth and a flat paddle-shaped tail that builds dams.
A small flying insect that gathers pollen and nectar to feed its colony.
A chewing insect with hardened protective front wing cases that shield delicate flight wings underneath.
A massive humped wild grazing bovine with shaggy brown fur that roams open grasslands.
A large wild ox with backward-curving horns that wallows in muddy rivers and marshes.
A flying insect with large colourful wings that develops from a caterpillar.
A desert animal with one or two humps that can go a long time without water.
A small yellow songbird famous for its bright plumage and melodious whistling voice.
A small carnivorous mammal with soft fur, retractile claws, and sharp night vision kept as a pet.
A plump crawling larval insect with a segmented body and multiple legs that feeds voraciously on leaves.
A slow-moving lizard that can change the colour of its skin.
The fastest land animal, a slender spotted cat built for sprinting.
A common farm bird kept for its eggs and meat that cannot fly far.
An intelligent tailless African great ape closely related to humans that uses tools and lives in social troops.
A highly venomous hooded serpent that flares its neck ribs outward when threatened.
A hardy flat-bodied scavenger insect that scurries rapidly through dark kitchens and crevices.
A large domestic grazing animal kept on farms for its milk and beef.
A highly adaptable North American prairie carnivore known for its nocturnal yipping howls and clever survival skills.
A shelled creature with ten legs and two big claws that walks sideways.
A large reptile with a long snout and powerful jaws that lurks in rivers.
A large intelligent black bird with a harsh cawing call.
A graceful hoofed animal of woods and fields whose males grow antlers.
A loyal domesticated carnivorous mammal widely kept as a devoted household pet and working companion.
A highly intelligent sea mammal famous for its playful leaps and clicking calls.
A domesticated hoofed mammal with long ears and a loud braying call used for riding and carrying loads.
A swift predatory aquatic insect with four transparent outstretched wings and huge faceted compound eyes.
A water bird with a broad flat bill and webbed feet that quacks.
A large powerful bird of prey with a hooked beak and keen eyesight.
A long ribbon-shaped fish that swims with continuous undulating wavelike movements through water.
A huge grey mammal with a long flexible nose and large tusks.
A slender domesticated burrower with a flexible tubular body and playful curious nature.
A soft-bodied nocturnal insect capable of producing rhythmic glowing flashes of light from its abdomen.
A tall pink bird with long thin legs that feeds in shallow salty lakes.
A small wild member of the dog family with a bushy tail and pointed ears.
A small tailless amphibian with long back legs that leaps and croaks near water.
A small delicate swift-footed African herbivore known for high stiff-legged leaps and curved ringed horns.
A small lizard with sticky toe pads that lets it climb walls and ceilings.
The tallest animal, with an extremely long neck and a patterned coat.
A sure-footed horned farm animal with a short beard that will eat almost anything.
A small orange freshwater fish commonly kept in home glass bowls and garden ponds.
A large web-footed waterbird known for its honking call and aggressive defensive hissing.
The largest ape, a powerful forest dweller that lives in family groups.
A plant-eating leaping insect possessing large muscular hind legs and sound-producing wing ridges.
A small stout tailless rodent from the Andes commonly raised as a gentle vocal household pet.
A small chubby rodent with stretchy cheek pouches, popular as a pet.
A small nocturnal mammal covered in sharp spines that rolls into a ball when scared.
An adult female domestic chicken kept on farms to lay edible eggs and raise chicks.
A long-legged freshwater wading bird that stands motionless in shallows before spearing fish with its bill.
A huge round African mammal that spends its days wallowing in rivers.
A large hoofed animal with a flowing mane that people have ridden for centuries.
A tiny brightly coloured bird that hovers in mid-air by beating its wings very fast.
A sloped-backed carnivorous mammal of Africa and Asia famous for its vocal cackling calls.
A large plant-eating lizard with a spiny crest along its back.
A compact muscular spotted big cat of the Americas that ambushes prey and swims well.
A soft see-through ocean animal with a bell-shaped body and stinging tentacles.
A large Australian marsupial that hops on powerful back legs and carries young in a pouch.
A young juvenile cat that playfully pounces on toys and drinks milk from its mother.
A tree-dwelling Australian marsupial with grey fur that feeds on eucalyptus leaves.
A colorful ornamental freshwater swimmer widely bred for decorative outdoor ponds and tranquil water gardens.
The largest living giant lizard that ambushes deer and water buffalo on isolated Indonesian islands.
A small round insect with a shiny red shell dotted with black spots.
A young woolly juvenile sheep that bleats softly and skips playfully across spring pastures.
A native primate of Madagascar with large reflective eyes, a pointed snout, and a long furry tail.
A powerful spotted wild cat that often drags its prey up into trees.
A large wild cat of Africa whose males have a thick shaggy mane.
A widespread scaly reptile typically possessing four legs, movable eyelids, and a long slender tail.
A long-necked South American pack animal with thick woolly fleece.
A large shelled sea creature with a long tail and big front claws, often eaten as a delicacy.
A small desert mammal that stands upright on its hind legs to guard its underground colony.
A small subterranean mammal with velvety dark fur and paddle-like front paws specialized for digging burrows.
A small agile carnivorous mammal renowned for its lightning reflexes and ability to fight venomous serpents.
A playful tree-dwelling primate with nimble hands and usually a long tail.
The largest member of the deer family, with broad flat antlers and a long face.
A small flying insect whose bite leaves an itchy bump on the skin.
A nocturnal insect with feathery antennae that is strongly drawn toward bright night artificial lights.
A tiny rodent with a pointed nose, round ears and a long thin tail.
A sturdy sterile hybrid equine beast widely used for packing heavy loads over steep mountain trails.
A soft-bodied sea creature with eight long limbs and a rounded head.
A large solitary long-armed ape covered in reddish-brown hair that lives high in Asian rainforest trees.
A large black and white apex marine mammal that hunts in intelligent coordinated family pods.
The largest living bird, which cannot fly but runs extremely fast on two long legs.
A playful furry mammal that swims in rivers and seas and eats fish.
A nocturnal bird of prey with large forward-facing eyes and silent flight.
A rare two-toned mammal from the mountain forests of central China.
A nocturnal insectivorous mammal covered in tough overlapping keratin plates that rolls into a tight ball.
A powerful dark-coated wild cat known for its silent nocturnal stealth in dense jungles.
A small slender seed-eating bird with a long tapering tail frequently kept in domestic cages.
A brightly coloured tropical bird with a curved beak that can mimic speech.
A large male bird famous for fanning out a shimmering tail of eye-patterned feathers.
A large water bird with a huge throat pouch on its long bill for scooping fish.
A flightless black and white seabird that swims expertly in cold southern seas.
A stout farm animal with a flat snout, often kept for its meat.
A plump grey bird common in city squares that coos and bobs its head.
A semiaquatic egg-laying Australian mammal with a broad snout, flattened tail, and venomous ankle spurs.
A huge white predator that roams the frozen far north hunting on sea ice.
A small domesticated equine characterized by a compact build, flowing mane, and gentle demeanor.
A large rodent covered in long sharp quills that it raises when threatened.
A playful juvenile dog known for boundless energy, curious behavior, and needle-sharp baby teeth.
A nonvenomous constricting tropical serpent that squeezes its prey in powerful muscular coils.
A small furry burrowing animal with long ears and a short fluffy tail.
A clever nocturnal mammal with a black mask-like face and a ringed tail.
A large intelligent black corvid with a deep croaking call that features prominently in mythology.
A massive thick-skinned grazing animal with one or two horns on its snout.
A familiar garden songbird recognized by its cheerful melody and reddish-orange breast feathers.
An adult male chicken recognized by its vibrant plumage, fleshy red head crest, and sunrise crow.
A slender moist-skinned tailed amphibian inhabiting damp forest leaf litter and shaded streams.
A silver migratory fish that swims up rivers against strong currents to lay eggs.
An eight-legged desert creature with pincers and a curved venomous tail.
A noisy white and grey bird of the coast known for stealing food from people.
A tiny marine fish with an upright curved posture and an equine head shape.
A sleek marine mammal with flippers that rests on shores and swims in cold waters.
A large predatory fish with rows of sharp teeth and a skeleton made of cartilage.
A woolly farm animal raised in flocks for its fleece and meat.
A black and white mammal that sprays a foul-smelling liquid when threatened.
A slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal that hangs upside down from branches.
A slow soft-bodied creature that carries a spiral shell on its back.
A long legless reptile that slithers along the ground and flicks its tongue.
A small plump brown and grey seed-eating bird that flocks abundantly in urban streets and gardens.
A small eight-legged creature that spins silk webs to trap insects.
A fast marine mollusk with an elongated body, large eyes, and eight arms plus two longer tentacles.
A small tree-climbing rodent with a big bushy tail that stores nuts.
A marine invertebrate with radiating limbs covered in tiny suckers found on tidal reefs.
A large long-legged wading bird famous in folklore for delivering newborn babies in cloth bundles.
A small agile migratory bird known for its forked tail and sweeping aerial acrobatics.
A large graceful water bird with a long curved neck, usually pure white.
A large predatory ocean swimmer characterized by an elongated sharp upper jaw resembling a blade.
The largest wild cat, with an orange coat marked by black stripes.
A dry-skinned warty terrestrial amphibian with short legs that hops along garden soil and woodland paths.
A slow-moving terrestrial reptile shielded by an arched dome-shaped bony shell into which it retracts.
A tropical rainforest bird known for its massive colorful curved bill.
A large fast ocean predator with streamlined silver sides widely harvested for canned food.
A reptile with a hard shell that lives mainly in water and swims with flippers.
A large scavenging bird with a featherless head that feeds on dead animal carcasses.
A large Arctic marine mammal with long tusks and a bristly moustache.
An enormous ocean mammal that breathes air through a blowhole and sings underwater.
A wild canine that lives and hunts in packs and howls at night.
A stocky burrowing Australian marsupial with short legs, a backward-facing pouch, and cubic feces.
A forest bird with a strong pointed beak used to drill into tree bark.
A long thin soft-bodied creature without legs that burrows through soil.
A long-haired domesticated bovine native to the high plateaus and cold mountains of Central Asia.
A wild African grazing animal whose coat is covered in bold dark bands.
